chapter: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band
title: How the alto horn prepared him for trumpet and reading
summary: He describes the alto horn's shape and size and says two years on it built his lip for trumpet and taught him to read.

bands.name: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Well, what does that alto horn look like, Jonah?
That's something like what I was telling you about, the upright bass. And then the baritone is next in size to it.
Yeah.
And then the alto horn is smaller.
So it's sort of the bell comes out like that?
No, the bell's straight up.
Oh, the bell's straight up.
Straight up, yeah.
I see what you mean, yeah.
And the baritone goes up like that too.
And the bass is straight up there too, see?
I see, yeah.
So they gave me this, and I stayed on it, I guess, about -- I stayed on it for two years.
Well, you learned to read.
Yeah, that was the great thing about it.
Yeah.
Because I still didn't realize what it meant. See an alto is to a trumpet player as a clarinet has a meaning to a saxophone.
To a saxophone.
See, you can get a good clarinet player and he can play the heck out of the saxophone.
Yeah.
But the other way around, no. A good tenor sax player, he wants to stay away from a clarinet.
That's right.
He won't be bothered with that. So that's why the alto kind of helps the trumpet out, because the mouthpiece is not big, but it's a little bigger than the trumpet, you know.
Yeah. So you can sort of ease into it.
Yes. And then by playing that alto for two years it gave me a nice -- it built up my muscles in my lip for the trumpet, and also made me know how to read good.
